Title: 1Code - Claude Code & Codex in One App | 21st
# A calm, visual client for parallel work. Claude Code and Codex in one app. Switch agents, take the best of each, ship with the best UI. ## One app, multiple agents. Switch between coding agents instantly. Use the right model for each task. ### Claude Code. ### Codex. OpenAI's cloud-native coding agent. Fast execution, parallel tasks, and broad model support. ## Three steps to shipping. Launch from the desktop app or the web. Open PRs, review diffs, and merge - all in one place. ## Ship code, not terminal commands. Everything you love about coding agents, with a visual interface designed for focused work. Work on multiple features at once. Each agent runs in its own session with full context. Plan mode, skills, message editing, and every feature your agent supports. ## Built-in Git, end to end. Stage, commit, diff, and open PRs without leaving the app. Git worktree isolation keeps every session clean. Stage files, review diffs, and commit with confidence. Open pull requests directly from the UI. Add descriptions, reviewers, and labels. Every agent session runs in its own git worktree. ## Agents that never sleep. Your agents keep running in isolated cloud sandboxes with live browser previews. Background agents continue working even when your laptop is closed. Every background session runs in an isolated cloud environment. See your dev branch running in a real browser. Toggle between desktop and mobile viewports. ## Connect anything with MCP. 1Code supports the MCP protocol. Plug in any MCP server - community or your own. Any MCP-compatible server works. Tag @1code in GitHub, Linear, or Slack to start an agent on demand. Auto-review PRs, fix CI failures, and complete Linear tasks. ### What is 1Code? ### Which coding agents are supported? ### Is 1Code open source? ### How does authentication work? ### How is 1Code different from the CLI? ### How is 1Code different from Claude Desktop? ### How is 1Code different from Conductor? ### What operating systems are supported? ### Is my code sent to your servers? ## Ready to ship faster? Built for developers who ship. ### Open Source. ### Max. Reach out at support@21st.dev or Discord.

results.content:
Title: Replicas: Run Claude Code and Codex in the cloud | Product Hunt
## Run Claude Code and Codex in the cloud. Spawn Claude Code or Codex in a VM with code and tooling ready to go. Hand off tasks from Slack, Linear, or GitHub Replicas runs Claude Code, Codex, or any coding agent in the cloud. Agents run in isolated VMs with real dev environments, and you can bring your own subscriptions and API keys. Trigger tasks from Slack, Linear, or GitHub and come back to a PR ready to review. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Replicas. Why we built this Like many of you, we think the future of software engineering is delegating to fleets of cloud agents. That means your agent stops the moment you close your laptop. What Replicas does Replicas runs your agents in isolated cloud VMs. Each one gets its own full dev environment, installs your dependencies, spins up your database, and runs your actual codebase locally inside the sandbox. It works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and more. Trigger it from wherever you already live: mention @replicas in a GitHub PR, ping it in Slack, assign a Linear issue, or hit the API. You come back to a PR ready to review. What we've seen We dogfood this hard: 95% of our own lifetime PRs were shipped with Replicas, and we haven't opened a single one without it in the last 3 months. This is just the beginning of what's possible when you can run agents in parallel, in the background, around the clock. The cloud VM approach makes sense especially when multiple agents need to run in the background without depending on someone's laptop. Replicas actually has a built in **feedback loop**, where it automatically reacts to CI failures, code reviews, and in this case merge conflicts. Spawn Claude Code in a VM with tooling ready to go, this is genuinely what I keep wishing existed when I'm. This is a huge benefit, because it means the features that the labs come up with are available right away — we don't have to wait months for the in-house harness to catch up.

results.content:
Title: Epho: Run Claude Code, Codex or Opencode in cloud with your repo | Product Hunt
## Run Claude Code, Codex or Opencode in cloud with your repo. Epho runs claude code, codex, or opencode in the cloud. Epho manages the underlying sandboxes, fallbacks, event streaming, and agent configuration for you. With a single API call, you can easily launch a Claude Code session that is already connected to your repo, understands your context, and runs in a serverless sandbox. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a review for Epho. I am super excited to launch a new agent primitive: Epho - run Claude Code in the cloud. 🚀 Epho is a cloud agent API: it allows you to spin up cloud sandboxes with Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode pre-configured. Epho came out of our own struggles with building our own AI analyst: - Sandboxes give you bare machines; you need to configure them for agentic workloads. We got to a point where things got quite reliable, and it became more obvious to us that this should be a primitive on its own: send a POST request, get the events streaming back to you. Epho is an agents-as-an-API product: you send a request, it spins up a sandbox, configures the chosen harness, clones your repos, and kicks off the agent. Epho uses your own keys, which means you only pay for the infrastructure Epho spins up for you. You send your Anthropic / OpenAI / Opencode API keys, and Epho uses them. You get $10 free if you sign up and verify your email, and you can run many hours of compute with that. You can use Opencode's free models to get started even without an API key and just play with it for free. For my code to run, the environment needs to have software installed (For example,. Feel free to drop me a note and we'll setup a special environment for you. Interesting approach with agents as an API and charging the infra per second instead of used tokens! @mad94 the tokens belong to you, and you run the agents with your own API key, that's why it didn't make much sense for us to charge you for tokens :).
